state.objective: Determine which client payroll and operating-expense COA repetitions are dimensions versus distinct natural expense natures. Preserve client reporting and do not compress merely to reach a target count.
confirmed_context: Unit/site is already a site_id dimension. Finance is centralized at HO.
Cost center may default from a unit for store postings but must remain extensible for HO departments and shared costs.
No payroll reports, statutory mappings, tax treatment, budgets, management P&L, capitalization policy, transactions or balances have been supplied.
Asset depreciation and inventory loss accounts were reviewed separately and are outside this question except where explicit unresolved replacement-OE expenses appear.
The purpose is to identify defensible compression candidates, not to approve migration from account names alone.

actual_client_patterns.payroll_26: Two parallel sets of the same 13 labels: salary, overtime, meal, transport, health, employee insurance/BPJS, THR, uniform, sport/recreation, funeral contribution, manpower development, severance, commission/bonus/incentive. The two sets use different legacy prefixes but the supplied extract does not explain whether they mean selling/admin, store/HO, department, or another function.
actual_client_patterns.replacement_oe_36: 36 Biaya Replacement OE accounts named by rack/display/table/mannequin/hanger and other OE item types.

payroll_duplicate_axis.instructions: Before merging the two parallel sets of 13 payroll accounts, must the client identify what the different legacy prefixes represent?

criteria.yes: Determine function, department, location, employee class, or another accounting/reporting distinction first.
criteria.retain: Parallel sets can never be merged.

payroll_26_to_13.instructions: If the two prefixes only encode department/function that can be reported reliably through cost_center/function, can 26 payroll GLs become 13 payroll natural accounts?

criteria.conditional_merge: Yes, preserve the 13 component natures and move department/function to dimensions.
criteria.retain_26: Keep both parallel sets even with reliable dimensional reporting.
criteria.one_payroll: Merge all 26 into one payroll expense GL.

all_payroll_one.instructions: Should salary, overtime, BPJS, THR, severance, bonuses and other payroll components all become one natural payroll expense account solely because payroll subledger has component detail?

criteria.no: Different statutory, tax, accrual, disclosure or management natures may justify separate natural accounts.
criteria.yes: One payroll expense account is always sufficient.
criteria.target: Choose based on desired COA count.

employee_identity.instructions: Should employee identity appear in natural GL accounts?

criteria.subledger: Use employee_id/payroll run in payroll subledger; post summarized GL by natural component and dimensions.
criteria.gl: Create a natural GL for every employee.
criteria.site: Use site account suffix as employee identity.

maintenance_assets.instructions: Can the ten maintenance/repair accounts be reduced to fewer Repairs & Maintenance GLs with asset_class/object detail when capitalization policy and management reporting are aligned?

criteria.conditional: Yes, asset/maintenance object belongs in asset_class or maintenance work order, subject to policy and reporting.
criteria.retain_10: Every maintained object must remain a GL.

software_maintenance.instructions: Should Software Maintenance automatically be merged with physical repairs solely because both contain maintenance?

criteria.review: Check service/subscription, capitalization and reporting treatment; it may warrant a separate nature.
criteria.merge: Always combine software and physical maintenance.

replacement_oe_items.instructions: If 36 Replacement OE labels only identify replaced item types, can item identity move to asset_id/item_class/work_order beneath fewer expense GLs?

criteria.conditional: Yes, after confirming expense versus capitalization and the reserve-replacement posting mechanism.
criteria.retain_36: Every OE item type must remain a natural expense GL.

utilities.instructions: Should electricity, water and telecommunications be merged into one Utilities GL solely because they are recurring services?

criteria.retain_or_policy: Keep distinct unless client reporting and policy support a broader utility account with service_type detail.
criteria.expense_dimension_only: Every expense type should be only a dimension under one expense GL.

vehicle_costs.instructions: Can tires, fuel/oil, vehicle licenses, vehicle insurance and vehicle repairs be collapsed into one Vehicle Cost GL from names alone?

criteria.no: Different nature, tax, timing and reporting can require separation; vehicle_id may supplement but does not erase nature.
criteria.yes: Vehicle object makes all costs the same nature.

bank_charges.instructions: Does moving bank identity to bank_account_id justify merging Bank Charges HO into unrelated operating expenses?

criteria.no: Bank identity can be dimensional while bank charges remain a distinct natural expense nature.
criteria.yes: Merge bank charges into miscellaneous expenses.
criteria.cash: Post bank charges directly to bank asset cost.

miscellaneous.instructions: Should Miscellaneous Expenses be used as the destination for many compressed expense accounts?

criteria.no: Use it narrowly with thresholds and review; preserve meaningful natures or controlled dimensions.
criteria.yes: Use it as the primary compression account.

lease_four.instructions: Can four lease/rent expense accounts be compressed before reviewing lease contracts and land-right accounting?

criteria.no: First determine short-term/low-value expense, right-of-use accounting, land rights and disclosure/reporting.
criteria.yes: All rent names can become one expense immediately.

migration_gate.instructions: What evidence is needed before final expense/payroll compression?

criteria.full: Management P&L and budget mapping, payroll/statutory reporting, tax treatment, sample postings, capitalization policy, opening balances and dimension-to-GL reconciliation.
